records.name: BIOMATH
records.scope_notes: Mathematical results and nonroutine mathematical methods for biosciences, or novel biological applications that identify a need for new mathematical approaches. Theory, simulation, biological networks and existing-data modelling can fit; a routine model application without substantive mathematical or biological contribution may not. Research articles undergo blind review by at least two independent reviewers.

route.conditions: The standard online route has no submission or processing fees and is free to readers. No selective waiver or author-affiliation requirement is stated. Printed copies and delivery are optional: an author requesting a physical copy must pay its postage. Use the journal's specified manuscript format.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the online route; optional printed-copy postage is outside that route.

fee_evidence.note: The funding policy explicitly excludes author submission and processing fees; online publication is free for authors and readers. Physical-copy postage is separately identified.
Current submission instructions repeat the no-submission/no-processing-fee policy without a waiver or affiliation condition.

difficulty.basis: No difficulty band assigned by diamond expansion; mathematical contribution criteria require manuscript-specific assessment.

records.name: Biometrical Letters
records.scope_notes: Statistical and mathematical methodology for life sciences, new statistical tools motivated by biological problems, and substantive applications or reviews of data-analysis methods. Existing biological datasets and simulation studies can fit. The journal encourages reproducible code and data and describes double-blind peer review.

route.conditions: Author instructions state that the journal costs nothing for authors or readers; no waiver, mandatory membership or affiliation restriction is stated. Submission is by email to the editorial office listed in those instructions. Prepare both identified and anonymous manuscript versions. Articles use a CC BY-NC-ND licence; check compatibility with funder requirements.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated under the blanket no-author-charge policy.

fee_evidence.note: The submission and review section states a journal-wide no-charge policy for authors and readers and immediate open access, rather than a selective APC waiver.

difficulty.basis: No acceptance-rate or difficulty assessment established by diamond expansion.

records.name: Biodiversity Informatics
records.scope_notes: Creation, integration, analysis and visualization of biodiversity information, including scholarly dataset work, assessments of information completeness, and software or protocol descriptions. Existing biodiversity datasets and substantive modelling/informatics advances fit; this is not a general molecular-bioinformatics journal. Research receives detailed peer review, normally with two anonymous reviewers.

route.conditions: The official policy explicitly makes submission and publication free. The author-information page describes no publishing-related fees of any kind. No selective waiver or membership requirement is stated. Authors register through the journal; current instructions require authenticated ORCID identifiers for all authors. Articles use a noncommercial Creative Commons licence.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None; the author-information policy excludes all fees related to journal publication.

fee_evidence.note: The official open-access policy explicitly excludes author charges for both submission and publication; author instructions also exclude page charges.
The journal describes its platinum model as having no fees of any kind connected with publishing scholarship.

difficulty.basis: No acceptance metrics or difficulty band established by diamond expansion; the journal expects a substantive contribution beyond routine use of existing models.

records.name: Peer Community Journal
records.publisher: Peer Community In; science sections web-published by Centre Mersenne
records.scope_notes: A multidisciplinary journal with a Mathematical and Computational Biology community and relevant genomics, ecology and evolutionary-biology communities. Theory, computer or mathematical models, existing-data studies and methodological work can fit the selected community. Articles must first complete the thematic Peer Community In review and recommendation process; the journal does not take an unevaluated manuscript directly.

route.conditions: The entire PCI evaluation and Peer Community Journal publication process is free for authors. Deposit a preprint in an appropriate open repository, submit it to a relevant thematic PCI, and obtain a recommendation before opting for journal publication. This is a scholarly review prerequisite, not a selective financial waiver. Open data/code requirements apply; authors prepare the final formatted article. Recommendation and acceptance are not guaranteed.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None charged by PCI or the journal; choose a free preprint/archive route for the required deposit.

fee_evidence.note: The publisher states that all stages of PCI and Peer Community Journal are free for authors and readers, and specifically confirms free transfer/publication of recommended articles.
The journal policy excludes author and reader fees, and explains prior PCI recommendation. Browser fetch returned 403, but a direct HTTPS request retrieved the policy page successfully with HTTP 200.

difficulty.basis: The relevant PCI must find a willing recommender and complete peer review; no acceptance probability or within-subfield difficulty band has been established.

records.name: Journal of Open Source Software
records.scope_notes: A cross-disciplinary research-software journal explicitly covering biology and scientific modelling/data analysis. A substantive, reusable computational-biology package can fit. Papers describe software and its research purpose rather than presenting new biological research results. Standalone notebooks, pretrained models and minor utility packages are outside the stated scope. Both software and the accompanying paper receive open external peer review.

route.conditions: Submission and publication are free. Software must use an OSI-approved open-source licence, have public source and development history, documentation and correctness checks, and satisfy current research-impact criteria. Current scope requires at least six months of public history. A submitting author must be a major contributor and participate through GitHub. A reviewed release must be archived with a DOI; choose a free archive. AI assistance requires disclosure and human validation under the current policy.
route.other_mandatory_costs: No journal fees; required software archiving can use a free service.

fee_evidence.note: The submission instructions explicitly state that neither submission nor publication carries a fee, and explain review and release archiving.
The official journal description confirms diamond open access and its zero-fee model, and states the current software-scope and review requirements.

difficulty.basis: Software maturity and research-impact criteria establish eligibility requirements, not an acceptance-rate estimate; no difficulty band assigned.

notes: Five additional journals, with no names duplicated from the computational-biology discovery file. All five have explicit current official no-author-fee policies covering the standard submission/publication route. Fee and ranking audits remain separate roles.

Scope is theoretical/computational biology, statistical methods for biological data, biodiversity information, or reusable research software. The entries do not propose clinical practice or new physical laboratory experiments.

Peer Community Journal requires prior thematic-PCI recommendation. That review prerequisite does not make the financial route a conditional waiver. The official PCI homepage currently lists Mathematical and Computational Biology, Genomics, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology among its communities. The mathematics/computational-biology community's own pages presented anti-bot errors; community existence was checked on the accessible publisher homepage.

Peer Community Journal's about page returned 403 in browser retrieval but was successfully read through a direct HTTPS request. The accessible PCI publisher homepage independently establishes that the entire process is free.

Biometrical Letters' current author guide contains unfinished template/copyright links. Its no-fee policy, society ownership, scope and peer-review statements are explicit; obtain the working templates from the editorial office when preparing an actual submission.
No preprint/repository records were added. Prior preprint deposits required by PCI remain dissemination steps, not evidence of journal peer review by themselves.

No citation metrics, processing-time promises, acceptance probabilities or difficulty bands were inferred. BIOMATH publishes official acceptance statistics on its about page; the ranking role should examine their years and denominator before using them.

Journal of Integrative Bioinformatics was not added: its current official publisher search result states an APC for unsolicited accepted articles. Historical free-publication descriptions should not be used as a current zero-fee policy.
Official pages checked on 2026-11-16. These are policy and scope checks, not human scientific review or an acceptance guarantee.
